problem.paragraph: Let $$B = \{\textbf{b}_{1} \text{,} \textbf{b}_{2}\}$$ and $$C = \{\textbf{c}_{1} \text{,} \textbf{c}_{2}\}$$ be bases for a vector space $$V$$ , and suppose $$\textbf{b}_{1} = 6\textbf{c}_{1} - 2\textbf{c}_{2}$$ and $$\textbf{b}_{2} = 9\textbf{c}_{1} - 4\textbf{c}_{2}$$ .

list.item: Find the change-of-coordinates matrix from $$B$$ to $$C$$ .
Find $$\left\lbrack \mathbf{x} \right\rbrack_{C}$$ for $$\textbf{x} = - 3\textbf{b}_{1} + 2\textbf{b}_{2}$$ . Use part (a).

problem.paragraph: Let $$B = \{\mathbf{b}_{1} \text{,} \mathbf{b}_{2}\}$$ and $$C = \{\mathbf{c}_{1} \text{,} \mathbf{c}_{2}\}$$ be bases for a vector space $$V$$ , and suppose $$\mathbf{b}_{1} = - \mathbf{c}_{1} + 4\mathbf{c}_{2}$$ and $$\mathbf{b}_{2} = 5\mathbf{c}_{1} - 3\mathbf{c}_{2}$$ .

list.item: Find the change-of-coordinates matrix from $$B$$ to $$C$$ .
Find $$\left\lbrack \mathbf{x} \right\rbrack_{C} \text{for} \mathbf{x} = 5\mathbf{b}_{1} + 3\mathbf{b}_{2}$$ .

problem.paragraph: Let $$U = \{\mathbf{u}_{1} \text{,} \mathbf{u}_{2}\}$$ and $$W = \{\mathbf{w}_{1} \text{,} \mathbf{w}_{2}\}$$ be bases for $$V$$ , and let $$P$$ be a matrix whose columns are $$\lbrack\mathbf{u}_{1}\rbrack_{W}$$ and $$\lbrack\mathbf{u}_{2}\rbrack_{W}$$ . Which of the following equations is satisfied by $$P$$ for all $$\mathbf{x}$$ in $$V$$ ?

list.item: $$\left[\right. x \left]\right._{U} = P \left[\right. x \left]\right._{W}$$
$$\left[\right. x \left]\right._{W} = P \left[\right. x \left]\right._{U}$$

problem.paragraph: Let $$A = \{\mathbf{a}_{1} \text{,} \mathbf{a}_{2} \text{,} \mathbf{a}_{3}\}$$ and $$D = \{\mathbf{d}_{1} \text{,} \mathbf{d}_{2} \text{,} \mathbf{d}_{3}\}$$ be bases for $$V$$ , and let $$P = \begin{bmatrix} \left\lbrack \mathbf{d}_{\mathbf{1}} \right\rbrack_{A} & \left\lbrack \mathbf{d}_{2} \right\rbrack_{A} & \left\lbrack \mathbf{d}_{3} \right\rbrack_{A} \end{bmatrix}$$ . Which of the following equations is satisfied by $$P$$ for all $$\mathbf{x}$$ in $$V$$ ?

list.item: $$\left[\right. x \left]\right._{A} = P \left[\right. x \left]\right._{D}$$
$$\left[\right. x \left]\right._{D} = P \left[\right. x \left]\right._{A}$$

problem.paragraph: Let $$A = \{\mathbf{a}_{1} \text{,} \mathbf{a}_{2} \text{,} \mathbf{a}_{3}\}$$ and $$B = \{\mathbf{b}_{1} \text{,} \mathbf{b}_{2} \text{,} \mathbf{b}_{3}\}$$ be bases for a vector space $$V$$ , and suppose $$\mathbf{a}_{1} = 4\mathbf{b}_{1} - \mathbf{b}_{2}$$ , $$\mathbf{a}_{2} = - \mathbf{b}_{1} + \mathbf{b}_{2} + \mathbf{b}_{3}$$ , and $$\mathbf{a}_{3} = \mathbf{b}_{2} - 2\mathbf{b}_{3}$$ .

list.item: Find the change-of-coordinates matrix from $$A$$ to $$B$$ .
Find $$\left\lbrack \mathbf{x} \right\rbrack_{B}$$ for $$\mathbf{x} = 3\mathbf{a}_{1} + 4\mathbf{a}_{2} + \mathbf{a}_{3}$$ .

problem.paragraph: Let $$D = \{\mathbf{d}_{1} \text{,} \mathbf{d}_{2} \text{,} \mathbf{d}_{3}\}$$ and $$F = \{\mathbf{f}_{1} \text{,} \mathbf{f}_{2} \text{,} \mathbf{f}_{3}\}$$ be bases for a vector space $$V$$ , and suppose $$\mathbf{f}_{1} = 2\mathbf{d}_{1} - \mathbf{d}_{2} + \mathbf{d}_{3}$$ , $$\mathbf{f}_{2} = 3\mathbf{d}_{2} + \mathbf{d}_{3}$$ , and $$\mathbf{f}_{3} = - 3\mathbf{d}_{1} + 2\mathbf{d}_{3}$$ .

list.item: Find the change-of-coordinates matrix from $$F$$ to $$D$$ .
Find $$\left\lbrack \mathbf{x} \right\rbrack_{D}$$ for $$\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{f}_{1} - 2\mathbf{f}_{2} + 2\mathbf{f}_{3}$$ .

exercise_group.instruction: In Exercises 7–10, let $$B = \{\mathbf{b}_{1},\mathbf{b}_{2}\}$$ and $$C = \{\mathbf{c}_{1},\mathbf{c}_{2}\}$$ be bases for $$\textbf{R}^{2}$$ . In each exercise, find the change-of-coordinates matrix from $$B$$ to $$C$$ and the change-of-coordinates matrix from $$C$$ to $$B$$ .

$$\mathbf{b}_{1} = \left[\right. \begin{matrix}- 1 \\ 8\end{matrix} \left]\right. , & \mathbf{b}_{2} = \left[\right. \begin{matrix}1 \\ - 5\end{matrix} \left]\right. , & \mathbf{c}_{1} = \left[\right. \begin{matrix}1 \\ 4\end{matrix} \left]\right. , & \mathbf{c}_{2} = \left[\right. \begin{matrix}1 \\ 1\end{matrix} \left]\right.$$

$$\mathbf{b}_{1} = \left[\right. \begin{matrix}- 6 \\ - 1\end{matrix} \left]\right. , & \mathbf{b}_{2} = \left[\right. \begin{matrix}2 \\ 0\end{matrix} \left]\right. , & \mathbf{c}_{1} = \left[\right. \begin{matrix}2 \\ - 1\end{matrix} \left]\right. , & \mathbf{c}_{2} = \left[\right. \begin{matrix}6 \\ - 2\end{matrix} \left]\right.$$

exercise_group.instruction: In Exercises 11–14, $$B$$ and $$C$$ are bases for a vector space $$V$$ . Mark each statement True or False (T/F). Justify each answer.

problem.paragraph: (T/F) The columns of the change-of-coordinates matrix $$\underset{C\leftarrow B}{P}$$ are $$B$$ -coordinate vectors of the vectors in $$C$$ .
(T/F) The columns of $$\underset{C\leftarrow B}{P}$$ are linearly independent.
(T/F) If $$V = \mathbb{R}^{n}$$ and $$C$$ is the standard basis for $$V$$ , then $$\underset{C\leftarrow B}{P}$$ is the same as the change-of-coordinates matrix $$P_{B}$$ introduced in Section 4.4.

(T/F) If $$V = \mathbb{R}^{2}$$ , $$B = \left\{ \mathbf{b}_{1},\mathbf{b}_{2} \right\}$$ , and $$C = \left\{ \mathbf{c}_{1},\mathbf{c}_{2} \right\}$$ , then row reduction of $$\begin{bmatrix} \text{c} _{1} & \text{c} _{ \text{2} } & \mathbf{b}_{1} & \mathbf{b}_{ \text{2} } \end{bmatrix}$$ to $$\begin{bmatrix} I & P \end{bmatrix}$$ produces a matrix $$P$$ that satisfies $$\left\lbrack \mathbf{x} \right\rbrack_{B} = P\left\lbrack \mathbf{x} \right\rbrack_{C}$$ for all $$\mathbf{x}$$ in $$V$$ .

In $$\text{ℙ} _{2}$$ , find the change-of-coordinates matrix from the basis $$B = \{ 1 - 2t + t^{2} \text{,} 3 - 5t + 4t^{2} \text{,} 2t + 3t^{2}\}$$ to the standard basis $$C = \{ 1 \text{,} t \text{,} t^{2}\}$$ . Then find the $$B$$ -coordinate vector for $$- 1 + 2t$$ .

In $$\text{ℙ} _{2}$$ , find the change-of-coordinates matrix from the basis $$B = \{ 1 - 3t^{2} \text{,} 2 + t - 5t^{2} \text{,} 1 + 2t\}$$ to the standard basis. Then write $$t^{2}$$ as a linear combination of the polynomials in $$B$$ .

exercise_group.instruction: Exercises 17 and 18 provide a proof of Theorem 15. Fill in a justification for each step.

problem.paragraph: Given $$\mathbf{v}$$ in $$V$$ , there exist scalars $$x_{1}, \text{…} ,x_{n}$$ , such that $$\mathbf{v} = x_{1} \mathbf{b}_{1} + x_{2} \mathbf{b}_{2} + \hdots + x_{n} \mathbf{b}_{n}$$

because (a) ________. Apply the coordinate mapping determined by the basis $$C$$ , and obtain $$\mathbf{\lbrack v\rbrack}_{C} = x_{1}\left\lbrack \mathbf{b}_{1} \right\rbrack_{C} + x_{2}\left\lbrack \mathbf{b}_{2} \right\rbrack_{C} + \cdots + x_{n}\left\lbrack \mathbf{b}_{n} \right\rbrack_{C}$$ because (b) ________. This equation may be written in the form $$\left\lbrack \mathbf{v} \right\rbrack_{C} = \left\lbrack {\left\lbrack \mathbf{b}_{1} \right\rbrack_{C} \left\lbrack \mathbf{b}_{1} \right\rbrack_{c} \cdots\left\lbrack \mathbf{b}_{\mathbf{n}} \right\rbrack_{C}} \right\rbrack\begin{bmatrix} x_{1} \\ \vdots \\ x_{n} \end{bmatrix}$$ by the definition of (c) ________. This shows that the matrix $$\underset{C\leftarrow B}{P}$$ shown in (5) satisfies $${\lbrack\mathbf{v}\rbrack}_{C} = \underset{C\leftarrow B}{P}{\lbrack\mathbf{v}\rbrack}_{B}$$ for each $$\mathbf{v}$$ in $$V$$ , because the vector on the right side of (8) is (d) ________.
Suppose $$Q$$ is any matrix such that $$\left\lbrack \mathbf{v} \right\rbrack_{C} = Q\left\lbrack \mathbf{v} \right\rbrack_{B}$$ for each $$\mathbf{v}$$ in $$V$$

Set $$\mathbf{v} = \mathbf{b}_{1}$$ in (9). Then (9) shows that $$\lbrack\mathbf{b}_{1}\rbrack_{C}$$ is the first column of $$Q$$ because (a) ________. Similarly, for $$k = 2,\ldots,n$$ , the $$k$$ th column of $$Q$$ is (b) ________ because (c) ________. This shows that the matrix $$\underset{C\leftarrow B}{P}$$ defined by (5) in Theorem 15 is the only matrix that satisfies condition (4).
